Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel-art SPRITE SHEET, one sheet of EXACTLY 8 separate full-body poses in a uniform 4-column by 2-row grid, canvas landscape 1536x1024, each cell 384x512. Reference image establishes the existing enemy identity: bony skeleton warrior with bare skull, ragged red scarf, steel sword and round wooden shield. Retain its colors, equipment and face silhouette, with detailed clean pixel art consistent with the game. Each pose faces LEFT in three-quarter side view. Top row four DISTINCT consecutive IDLE poses: subtle arm/weapon movement and cloth or moss/tendrils shifting, same body height, no breathing squash. Bottom row four consecutive ATTACK poses: 1 raises sword to prepare, 2 winds back sword, 3 slashes LEFT while shielding, 4 follows through ready to recover. Keep ALL parts, weapons, arrows and effects entirely inside their own cell, generous transparent gaps of at least 40 px around each pose. Same scale and ground baseline within every cell. Absolutely NO crossing cell boundaries, no cropping, no labels, no grid lines. Background MUST be genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha, no black backdrop, no shadows or floor. All eight frames must be visibly different and usable for animation.
CRITICAL SPACING CORRECTION: Draw every character SMALLER. Within EACH 384x512 cell, ALL visible pixels must fit in a central bounding box NO MORE THAN 220 pixels WIDE and 310 pixels HIGH, including the ENTIRE weapon at maximum extension. That means minimum 82px empty alpha margin on left/right of EVERY cell and minimum 80px above/below. DO NOT fill cells. Keep characters small with wide gaps even during attack. NO slash trails, NO emitted projectile arrows, NO flying debris, NO detached particles: only the character and held equipment, compact poses. The shadow wraith's tendrils must stay compact. Preserve all eight distinct poses. Treat it as an animation data sheet, not an art poster. Do not scale up characters to fill blank space.
